title: Sales Enablement: Unified Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core sales enablement artifacts into a single reference for AEs, SDRs, solution engineers, and partner reps. It covers: positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, a recommended pitch-deck structure with talking points, practical pricing guidance and negotiation levers, two short customer case study vignettes, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects. Use this document as the canonical source for customer conversations and presales collateral.

1) Positioning & Messaging (elevator → why now → value props)

- Elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-effective LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams ship LLM features without building and operating complex inference stacks.

- Why now:
  1. Models are rapidly evolving; serving is where operational differentiation happens.
  2. Teams need predictable latency, cost control, and flexible deployment (hosted → dedicated → private) as usage and compliance needs grow.
  3. Open model ecosystems make runtime optimizations and routing policies a key lever for unit economics.

- Key value props (primary):
  - Production-first serving runtime: high-throughput GPU-optimized inference with KV-caching and continuous batching for predictable latency and lower per-token costs.
  - Unified API & tooling: same API/rollout/config across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem).
  - Cost-aware controls: batching, caching, quantization profiles, and routing policies with measurable cost impact.
  - Reliability & graceful degradation: multi-tier fallbacks (model variants, regions, capacity tiers) and SLA-backed Dedicated offerings.

- Messaging guidance by persona:
  - Engineering/ML: emphasize runtime technical benefits (kernel selection, quantization profiles, KV cache, low p99 latency, perf benchmarks).
  - Platform/SRE: emphasize observability, token-level cost/latency breakdown, rollout automation, and error budgets.
  - Product/PM: emphasize integration speed, structured outputs, function/tool calling, and predictable economics.
  - Security/Compliance: emphasize Private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC/ISO evidence.

2) Competitive Briefs (1-page cheat sheets)

- Competitive landscape summary (three categories):
  - Managed API-first providers (fast onboarding, less ops control).
  - Cloud AI endpoint services (tight cloud integration, variable performance/cost).
  - Self-hosted inference runtimes/orchestration vendors (high control, more operational burden).

- Direct competitive differentiators (how to position Redwood vs each):
  - Versus API-first providers: "You get the simplicity of a hosted API plus the ability to move to dedicated/private when you need predictable capacity, security, or lower unit cost."
  - Versus cloud endpoint services: "We provide model- and hardware-aware runtime optimizations and better per-token economics through batching/caching — and consistent API across clouds and private deployments."
  - Versus self-hosted vendors: "We offer an opinionated, production-ready runtime with built-in tooling, observability, and enterprise features so your team doesn’t have to build the orchestration and performance tuning yourself."

- Quick competitor feature comparison (example table):

| Capability | Redwood | API-first | Cloud Endpoints | Self-hosted Runtime |
|---|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Fast onboarding | Yes | Yes | Partial | No |
| Dedicated capacity / SLA | Yes | No | Partial | Yes (ops) |
| Private / on-prem | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Observability + cost breakdown | Yes | Partial | Partial | Varies |
| Built-in batching/caching | Yes | No | Partial | Varies |

- Top objections & rebuttals:
  - "We can host ourselves to save money." → "Building an ops-grade inference platform takes months/years; our dedicated/private options and Optimize toolkit typically reduce TCO and speed time-to-value. We also surface quantization and batching profiles tailored to your workload to realize cost savings."
  - "We’re already on a cloud provider's AI endpoints." → "Cloud endpoints vary by region and lack consistent cross-environment tooling; we provide predictable performance and a path to private deployments for regulated workloads."

3) Pitch Deck — recommended structure & speaker notes

- Slide 1: Title / One-line value prop
- Slide 2: Agenda / Customer pain (latency/cost/ops)
- Slide 3: Why now — market context
- Slide 4: Redwood product overview (hosted, dedicated, private)
- Slide 5: How it works at a high level (serving runtime + orchestration)
- Slide 6: Key differentiators (performance, unified API, cost controls, private)
- Slide 7: Architecture diagram (hosted → dedicated → private routing)
- Slide 8: Benchmarks / performance profiles (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens)
- Slide 9: Pricing & packaging summary (highlighting discounting levers and reserved capacity)
- Slide 10: Case studies / references (short wins)
- Slide 11: Security & compliance summary
- Slide 12: Next steps & recommended pilot

Speaker notes highlights:
- Emphasize measurable economics: show how batching/caching/quantization reduced cost in examples (e.g., 30–60% cost reduction depending on workload).
- For enterprise buyers, lead with Dedicated and Private options and SLA commitments.
- Call out rollout plan: start hosted pilot -> dedicated reserve -> private migration if needed.

4) Pricing guidance & negotiation levers

- Pricing model overview:
  - Hosted API: usage-based (per-token for generation and per-unit for embeddings).
  - Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved capacity with SLA and committed throughput.
  - Private: license/installation and optional support contract.

- Standard tiers (guidance table):

| Tier | Typical customer | Billing model | Key commitment | Expected discount vs hosted |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Self-serve Hosted | PoC / early product teams | Pay-as-you-go | No commit | 0% |
| Growth / Dedicated | High-volume apps | Monthly/Annual reservation | 3–24 month commit | 10–35% |
| Enterprise / Private | Regulated & large orgs | License + support | 12–36 month contract | 25–50% |

- Negotiation levers (what you can offer):
  - Committed volume discounts (increase with term length and volume).
  - Pilot programs: 3-month hosted pilot with success metrics and credits for conversion.
  - Professional services: accelerated onboarding, quantization/model tuning, performance optimization.
  - Observability retention / premium SLAs: add-on priced per GB or per-app.

- Pricing red flags (avoid unscoped entitlements):
  - Unclear definition of tokens (ensure same tokenization baseline).
  - Unlimited low-latency SLOs without defined usage caps (use tiers).

5) Case studies (2 short vignettes for slides / one-pagers)

- Case study A — FinTech fraud detection (Growth customer):
  - Problem: Real-time transaction scoring required p99 latency < 120ms and strict data residency.
  - Solution: Dedicated deployment in region + KV prefix caching and optimized batching.
  - Outcome: p99 improved from 220ms → 95ms, cost per 1M tokens down 28%, compliance met via Private-ready deployment contracts.
  - Owner / reference: Customer success: Priya Singh; Technical lead: Noah Chen.

- Case study B — Marketplace personalization (PLG scale):
  - Problem: High throughput embedding generation with unpredictable burst traffic and tight unit-cost targets.
  - Solution: Hosted + autoscaling Dedicated burst pool, Optimize recommendations (quantization profile + batching).
  - Outcome: Throughput increased 3x during peak windows; monthly inference bill reduced 35% after tuning.
  - Owner / reference: Growth AE: Liam O'Connor; Solutions Eng: Sofia Patel.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short, customer-facing answers)

Q: How is my data protected?
A: We provide industry-standard protections: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, role-based access controls, and audit logging. For sensitive workloads, Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) ensure data never leaves customer-controlled networks; we support KMS/HSM integrations for key management.

Q: Can you support regulatory requirements (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR)?
A: Yes. We offer data residency controls, audit logs, and contractual addenda (DPA). For HIPAA workloads we recommend Private deployments and a scoped BAA — engage our security team early.

Q: Who can access logs and prompts?
A: Access is controlled by RBAC and audit logs. By default, hosted logs are accessible to Redwood SRE for support per customer consent; enterprise customers can opt for private control plane where logs remain in the customer environment.

Q: What certifications / evidence do you provide?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestations (evidence shared under NDA). We provide architecture diagrams, penetration test summaries, and SLA docs as part of enterprise diligence.

Q: How do you secure model weights and third-party models?
A: Model artifacts can be stored in encrypted object stores. For private deployments, model artifacts are under customer control. We maintain a model onboarding security checklist for third-party models that includes provenance checks and license compliance.

Q: What is your incident response process?
A: We have a documented incident response playbook, SRE oncall rotations, and a customer communication plan tied to our status page. For Dedicated and Private customers we provide escalation contacts and runbooks as part of the onboarding package.

7) Presales playbook: recommended pilot -> conversion flow

- Pilot characteristics (recommended):
  - Duration: 30–90 days (90 for enterprise compliance scopes).
  - Success metrics: p99 latency target, cost-per-1M-token target, throughput target, feature completeness (API integration + structured outputs).
  - Team: AE, Solution Engineer, Customer Success, Security reviewer (if required).

- Steps (numbered):
  1. Discovery: capture technical constraints, compliance needs, traffic profile, and success metrics.
  2. Proposal: recommend hosted pilot or dedicated reserved pool with reference pricing and success milestones.
  3. Onboard: provide quickstart templates, a test corpus, and a tuning checklist (quantization, batching).
  4. Optimize: run Optimize toolkit recommendations and measure gains (expect 20–40% cost reductions commonly).
  5. Review & convert: present results, propose committed capacity or Private deployment if needed.

Appendix: Quick response lines for common sales threads

- "Can you match competitor X's price?" → "We can align on committed volumes/term; let's evaluate the workload and propose a tailored reserved capacity plan that demonstrates TCO improvements."
- "How long to go from PoC to production?" → "Typical timeline: 2–8 weeks for a hosted-to-dedicated rollout depending on integration complexity and compliance needs."

Document maintenance: update this playbook quarterly or when major product/contract changes occur. For updates, contact the document owner (Sofia Patel) or submit edits via the sales-enablement channel.

End of playbook.
